Under the explicitly named source inputs, the sum of Phi(rho_k(y)/y) is o(k) if and only if every positive orbit is eventually periodic. - Every positive target coprime to three is reached simultaneously by $x,3x$ in exactly 14 shortcuts and by $x,3x,9x$ in exactly 28. The base may depend on the target. Targets 439 and 475963 respectively rule out every shorter universal clock. A separate explicit infinite family of odd triples first reaches 1 at the common time $21+1458t$. [Sharp clocks and family](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/640bf7e511831a0ffc4f00462f12df81f8a8a619/research/clock-itineraries/FreeTowerFamilies.md)

With Mazur’s positive lower density as an explicit input, the bases visiting each fixed unit target have positive lower natural density. Universal convergence is then equivalent to finding arbitrarily large stages with arbitrarily small missed fractions for one gate and one deadline at each stage. Bařina’s finite verification already supplies a common deadline below the explicit stage bound $9\cdot 2^{43}$. [Density transfer](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/640bf7e511831a0ffc4f00462f12df81f8a8a619/research/clock-itineraries/SynchronousDensityTransfer.lean) · [Gate criterion](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/640bf7e511831a0ffc4f00462f12df81f8a8a619/research/clock-itineraries/SynchronousBasinDensity.lean) · [Finite baseline](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/640bf7e511831a0ffc4f00462f12df81f8a8a619/research/clock-itineraries/SynchronousFiniteRange.lean) · [Mazur, Theorem 1.1](https://www.proofatlas.ai/papers/positive-lower-density-collatz-predecessors/paper-v1.pdf) · [Bařina, 2025](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11227-025-07337-0)

- Every Mersenne exponent has a canonical representative $Y$ whose triple reaches 1 in exactly three odd departures. The orbit of $Y$ meets the prescribed Mersenne orbit. Among 192 specified hard sources, 183 have certified smaller canonical parents. All 183 meetings lie in the new PR 201 short-clock cone. For the first delayed source, two different integer replays give first hitting time 27,198,220. [Fixed-source results](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/640bf7e511831a0ffc4f00462f12df81f8a8a619/research/clock-itineraries/ReturnDescent.md) · [Fresh PR 201](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/3376695869fcf7d2e34f676a876d2b78a391d799/research/six-hour-20261127/coupling/PEAK_RIGIDITY.md)

Both natural witnesses in PR 201 have exponentially growing denominators on a fixed source. A separate written proof for the Bergman transfer gives an operator distance equal to zero under convergence and the full norm if another component exists. The analytic identification is a written proof. Its row arithmetic and real suprema have Lean proofs. At stage $X>1$, at least $\lfloor X/D\rfloor$ distinct synchronized bases reach gate 1 within $6+10.46\log X$ further shortcuts from their common 28-step endpoint. <details><summary>Reproduce the four finite gate counts with Python</summary>

```python
from array import array
import time
start=time.monotonic()
cap=1<<22
dist=array('H',[0])*cap
dist[1]=1
def time_to_one(x):
    trail=[]
    while x>=cap or not dist[x]:
        trail.append(x)
        x=(3*x+1)//2 if x%2 else x//2
        if len(trail)>4096: raise ValueError('unresolved trajectory')

    for n in reversed(trail):
        h+=1

u=0
deadline=0
```

<details><summary>Earlier proposal and verification history</summary>

**The Collatz conjecture remains open.** This draft proves an unconditional statement about ordinary Collatz trajectories and uses it to give an exact criterion for universal convergence. The source review covers the frozen research entry points of PRs #160 through #209. [Mathematical proposal](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/November25.md) · [Index of 50 source PRs](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/FiftyPRs.md)

## A theorem about powers of three

Fix an odd positive integer `w` and any starting rank `s`. There is an offset `d ≤ 2^1379` such that all 513 integers `3^(s+d+r) * w`, for `0 ≤ r ≤ 512`, have the same value after exactly 1,381 shortcut Collatz steps. That value is smaller than the first input in the block. [Lean merger theorem](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/TowerFrontierMergers.lean) · [Construction and bounds](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/TowerFrontier.md)

Call rank `r` a change if exactly one of `3^r * w` and `3^(r+1) * w` reaches 1. Lean proves that Collatz is equivalent to the following statement. Whenever an odd tower has a change at rank zero, every interval of 512 consecutive ranks contains a change. The common-endpoint theorem supplies an interval with 512 consecutive equalities. The missing step is to prove that a change at the prescribed starting rank would have to recur in that interval. For any fixed rank and deadline, arbitrarily large odd bases have adjacent orbit segments disjoint through that deadline. [Tripling descent and recurrence criterion](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/TowerRecurrence.lean) · [Prescribed-rank obstruction](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/TowerFrontierPrescribed.lean)

A fixed deadline cannot transfer a witness for reaching 1 to every later tower rank. Every shortcut step satisfies `n ≤ 2*T(n)`. After `t` steps this gives `n ≤ 2^t*T^t(n)`. Consequently, if `3^r*w > 2^H`, that rank cannot reach 1 by time `H`. For example, 5 and `3^4*5 = 405` have the same first four parity bits. Their fourth iterates are 1 and 76. The bound and the example were checked separately in Lean against the same published modules.

## Other approaches to the full conjecture

- A supplied odd orbit coprime to three eventually repeats exactly when its coefficients `3^k / 2^(S_k)` stay bounded, where `S_k` counts the shortcut steps through its first `k` odd gaps. Universal pointwise boundedness together with arbitrarily late negative results from the finite cycle test is equivalent to Collatz. Both claims remain open. [Combined theorem](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/NovemberProposal.lean) · [Pointwise theorem](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/EscapeRecords.lean)
- Finite counts of misses in intervals `[X,2X)` can certify convergence to 1, including convergence of the common target used in the count. Successful tests at arbitrarily large scales would prove Collatz. [Counting argument and finite examples](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/WindowCapture.md)
- An escaping orbit would spend at least `17/41` of its odd times in lower asymptotic density in 403 of the 4,374 unit classes modulo `3^8`. The cycle argument gives lower bounds on the number of high phases of a hypothetical cycle under the three explicit numerical hypotheses documented in the proof. [Escaping-orbit restrictions](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/EscapeFrontier.md) · [Cycle restrictions and hypotheses](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/CycleFrontier.md)

All 28 Lean modules rebuilt with native Lean 4.34.1 from a clean checkout at `45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09` with an initially empty project export directory. [Build order and replay commands](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/45a6a111321f947a8482c9e96e898435b57cee09/research/clock-itineraries/README.md)

<summary>Earlier proofs included in this branch</summary>

### Earlier clock criterion and finite search

The ordinary positive-integer Collatz conjecture is equivalent to the conjunction of two arithmetic statements. Both remain open. This draft supplies proofs of the equivalence, a pointwise recurrence certificate, and a finite Boolean cycle test. [Mathematical proposal](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/b2b56b94175174a680a296478f16c619a8828972/research/clock-itineraries/Proposal.md) · [Final Lean theorem](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/b2b56b94175174a680a296478f16c619a8828972/research/clock-itineraries/FinalProposal.lean)
